A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete, readable 32-page versions of SafeVLA, including Appendices A–H. Text comparison and page rendering support reliable comparison of all material.

before.justification: v3 reports original benchmark experiments measuring task success and safety costs in Section 5, sim-to-real observations, and additional empirical analyses in Appendices A–B.

after.justification: v4 retains these original experimental outcomes, including the benchmark results in Table 1, sim-to-real observations, and appendix analyses.

M1.justification: The ISA pipeline, safety predicates, constrained learning objective, and policy/multiplier updates in Sections 3–4 and Appendices C–D are identical.

E1.justification: Both retain the same Safety-CHORES tasks, navigation benchmarks, DivScene evaluation, perturbation and extreme-failure scenarios, and sim-to-real Safety-PickUp evaluation.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains FLaRe, FLaRe-RS, SPOC variants, and navigation-only Poliformer. Comparator membership in the other experiments also matches.

E3.justification: Training budgets, data splits, evaluation scene counts, observation/action settings, SR/CC metrics, and perturbation protocols in Section 5.1 and Appendices C/E are unchanged.

E4.justification: The risk-elicitation, penalty-coefficient and cost-threshold ablations, extreme-failure tests, and supplementary behavioral, generalization and convergence analyses are unchanged.

E5.justification: Appendix A retains the same logistic-regression, correlation and significance-reporting procedures, including the 1% significance threshold. No run-count, seed or uncertainty-reporting information changes.

E6.justification: All reported numerical and qualitative results match. For example, Table 1 reports ISA Safety-ObjNav SR 0.865 and CC 1.854 in both versions; appendix outcomes are also unchanged.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, safety-predicate formalizations, and optimization/update Equations (1)–(10) are unchanged. No assumptions, derivations or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the same ISA/Safety-CHORES novelty claims and claims concerning safety improvements, maintained task performance and generalization.

C2.justification: Interpretations of safety–performance tradeoffs and risk handling are unchanged, as are Appendix G's limitations concerning simulation reliance, trajectory-level credit assignment and uniform binary constraints.

D1.justification: The hyperparameters, software, hardware, constraint pseudocode and evaluation details in Appendices C–E are unchanged. Code/data/model access and licensing statements also match.

R1.justification: Section 2, Appendix F and the bibliography retain the same cited works and positioning relative to VLA training, SafeRL and robotics safety.

P1.justification: v4 adds Yishuai Cai as an author, revises affiliation superscripts, adds Zhongguancun Academy, and updates the arXiv version/date stamp. Research prose, headings and document organization are unchanged.

P2.justification: All figures, tables, captions and placements are unchanged; pages 2–32 render identically. Page 1 retains the same layout despite its author, affiliation and stamp text edits.

improvement.justification: Only authorship, affiliation and arXiv front matter change. Scientific methods, evidence, claims, limitations and reproducibility information remain identical, with no meaningful net difference in overall paper quality.
